title: Wisdom
lead: In the Bible wisdom (Hebrew chokhmah) is skill for living: practical, moral and religious good sense that begins with the fear of the LORD. It is a craftsman's skill, a judge's insight and a teacher's art, and in Proverbs and later writings Wisdom is pictured as a woman beside God at creation.

sections.b: The Hebrew word chokhmah covers many skills: the craftsmen who make the tabernacle are "wise of heart" (Exodus 31:3–6), a wise woman of Tekoa talks David round (2 Samuel 14:2), and Solomon's wisdom is first shown as justice in a hard court case (1 Kings 3:16–28) and then as knowledge of plants and animals and proverbs (1 Kings 4:29–34). The wisdom books, Proverbs, Job and Ecclesiastes, teach that the fear of the LORD is where wisdom begins (Proverbs 9:10) and test that teaching against suffering and death. Proverbs 8 pictures Wisdom beside God before creation, an idea taken further in the Wisdom of Solomon and Sirach. The New Testament calls Christ "the wisdom of God" (1 Corinthians 1:24, 30) and says that something more than Solomon is here (Matthew 12:42).
